evidence.computation: For row-gauge requests, rows equal gauge row count divided by gauge span, times target length after inch/cm conversion, rounded to the nearest integer with ties to even. The kernel refuses a nonpositive gauge span or negative row count or length. Other crafts requests retain their own named convention. Quilt blocks use exact rational floor in both dimensions, so each count fits and one additional block in that direction does not. Named full digital RGB channels combine by channel union; every returned channel occurs in an input and every input channel is retained. Continuous fabric length converts exactly to yards without whole-yard purchase rounding.
assumptions: Row-gauge requests assume uniform gauge across the requested length.
RGB composition uses saturated full digital channels. It does not predict weighted brightness, spectra or paint mixtures.
Fabric conversion assumes one continuous length with no width, waste or discrete cutting model.
untrusted: English quantity roles, source unit recognition and output rendering.

evidence.computation: Drywall sheet and stair riser counts use exact rational ceiling. The returned sheet count covers the net area and one fewer sheet does not. Board-foot answers equal the exact rectangular volume in cubic inches times the whole piece count divided by144; dimensions are converted in HOL from inch, foot, centimetre or millimetre source tags, and dimensions/count are nonnegative.
assumptions: The stated area, openings and sheet size are the intended quantities; no waste allowance is inferred.
The supplied dimensions describe rectangular complete pieces; no nominal-to-dressed correction or waste allowance is inferred.
Bare thickness and width in conventional dimension products use inches; length requires a supplied unit. Partial-board quantities remain unsupported.
Piece-count word grammar supports zero through ninety-nine; other explicit quantities or grouped counts are withheld rather than defaulted to one.
untrusted: English quantity/unit recognition and real-project applicability of the stated model.

evidence.computation: Exact length conversion followed by the least integral layer count covering a nonnegative part height with positive uniform layer height.
assumptions: Uniform layer height; no separate first layer, adaptation or machine offset.
untrusted: English quantity roles, source unit recognition and output rendering.

evidence.computation: For occupant counts, exact rational ceiling covers the area under the stated or named table load factor; one fewer occupant allocation does not.
assumptions: The selected load factor and named code-table convention apply to the supplied arithmetic problem.
untrusted: English recognition and applicability of the selected physical/code convention.

evidence.computation: The requested NIOSH weight limit or lifting index remains explicit. A lifting index requires load and positive weight limit. Inputs require nonnegative distances, angle and load, frequency multiplier in [0,1], and coupling multiplier 0.90, 0.95 or 1.00. Under these necessary bounds the arithmetic weight limit lies in [0,23] kg; the index times weight limit equals the supplied load.
assumptions: The NIOSH lifting equation applies to the supplied task.
The user supplied the correct frequency and coupling table entries for task conditions; guards do not select or verify the applicable row.
Geometry uses centimetres, load kilograms and angle degrees under the named metric convention.
untrusted: Exact numeral lexing, English quantity roles and units, JSON framing.
